newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: U.N. aid agencies return to Tajikistan.
newsitem.headline: U.N. aid agencies return to Tajikistan.

text.p: U.N. aid agencies, which left Tajikistan in February after some of their staff were taken hostage by an armed band, are now returning to the war-ravaged country, a U.N. worker said on Monday.

"Last Friday heads of missions of the five U.N. agencies which left Tajikistan during the hostage crisis returned to the capital Dushanbe," Richard Mordzjinsky, a political affairs officer at the United Nations mission, told Reuters.
"The return was possible due to improvement of the security situation in Tajikistan," Mordzjinsky said.
He said the staff of the agencies, which included the UNHCR refugee agency, UNICEF children's fund and UNDP development programme, had started returning from the Uzbek capital Tashkent.

Aid agencies helping impoverished Tajikistan to overcome the consequences of a bloody civil war left the former Soviet republic after an armed group seized 15 hostages, including several U.N. workers, Russian reporters and the Tajik security minister, in February.
The hostages were held captive for two weeks and released only after the government met all the conditions set by the kidnappers.
Last month the rebel group was crushed in a military operation carried out by the secular government together with the country's united Islamist opposition.
The government and opposition are worried that a ceasefire agreed last December to put an end to a four-year civil war may be disrupted by maverick bands.
A representative of the U.S. embassy said that because of the more stable situation in Tajikistan, Washington had cancelled a February 20 order to families of U.S. diplomats to leave Dushanbe.
The decision was prompted by the hostage crisis and the killing of two embassy security guards. The guards were locally-hired ethnic Russians who were off-duty at the time.
The mission of the International Committee of the Red Cross, which also suspended aid to Tajikistan during the hostage crisis, could not be immediately reached for comment.

In an attempt to promote peace talks, President Imomali Rakhmonov said on Monday he was ready to meet the leader of the Islamist opposition, Sayid Abdullo Nuri, before a new round of talks in Tehran scheduled for May 16.
A foreign ministry spokesman said this was likely to provide "a new, powerful impetus" to the peace process.
The talks, mediated by the United Nations, were suspended earlier this month to give the two delegations time for consultations with their respective leaderships.
